writeup.headline: Shopify rates Buy on strong growth and a net-cash balance sheet, but sits just above Hold.
writeup.thesis: Shopify scores 66, a Buy with medium confidence, only 2 points above the Hold line at 65. The rating is carried by growth (81), with revenue up 33.69% year on year in the latest quarter and 32.5% on a trailing basis, and by a balance sheet scoring 100 thanks to net cash and no reported debt. Quality (68) is solid, with a 17.73% free cash flow margin, a 13.9% operating margin and a slightly shrinking share count, while trend (75) shows the price 33.09% above its 200-day average and 3.75% off its 52-week high. Valuation (31) is the main drag: in absolute terms the multiples are high, at 16.874 times sales, 95.193 times free cash flow and 118.735 times EV/EBIT, with a free cash flow yield 4.16 points below the 10-year Treasury yield. Against its own history the stock is labelled cheap, with P/FCF cheaper than at 45 of the last 61 month-ends and EV/EBIT cheaper than at 51 of the last 61 month-ends, while P/S is near the middle of the last 61 month-ends (cheaper than at 34, more expensive than at 26).
key_risks: The score is within 2 points of Hold, so a small slip in any factor could change the rating.
Absolute valuation is high (P/FCF 95.193, EV/EBIT 118.735), leaving little room for disappointment.
Growth is easing slightly, with acceleration at -0.63 points.

Q3 results are due November 3, 2026; the news ratings were not refreshed this run, and the Briskin privacy class action remains unresolved.
what_would_change: A drop of more than 1 point in the composite, for example from slowing growth or a weaker trend score, would move the rating to Hold.
